profile.unsupportedTooltip: Uses script directives the interactive service refuses for unauthorised callers
profile.unsupportedTooltip@macos: Uses script directives, which the helper refuses on macOS because OpenVPN runs as root there
profile.unsupportedNotice: This profile uses script directives. The interactive service refuses those for callers that are not authorised.
profile.unsupportedNotice@macos: This profile uses script directives. On macOS OpenVPN runs with root rights, so the helper refuses every directive that would run a program, and this profile cannot be connected.
profile.deleteConfirm: Delete '{0}' permanently? Its history goes with it, and it is stopped first if it is connected.
profile.compressionRefused: This server pushed a compression setting, and a current OpenVPN client cannot apply any of them, including one that turns compression off. It refuses the whole set of pushed options instead, which is why the tunnel never comes up. Ignoring the setting with a pull filter is not a way around it: the tunnel then connects and carries nothing, because the server compresses what the client no longer expects. Only the server can fix this, by not pushing compression.
profile.defaultRouteRefused: The server asked to carry all traffic. This profile ignores that, so the host keeps its own default route. Change it in the profile if the tunnel is meant to carry everything.
profile.signInAgainHint: Forgets the credentials stored for this profile so the next connection asks for them. Use it when the password changed on the server.
profile.pingViaTunnel: Measured against the tunnel gateway {0}, so this is the round trip through the tunnel.
profile.pingViaServer: This server names no tunnel gateway, so the round trip is measured against the server itself at {0}, over the ordinary route rather than through the tunnel.

reason.pushedCompressionRefused: The server pushed a compression setting this client cannot apply, so it refused every option the server sent.
reason.connectTimedOut: The tunnel did not come up within {0} seconds.
reason.credentialsRejected: The credentials for '{0}' were rejected by the server.
reason.unknown: The connection ended for a reason this version cannot name.

settings.languageHint: Language files live beside the application and in the lang folder under the application data directory. Drop a JSON file there and reload to add a language without a new build.
settings.closeToTray: Closing the window keeps the tunnels running
settings.profileEditorHint: Either is one button away in the editor. This decides which one appears first.
settings.autoStartFailed: The autostart entry could not be changed. The other settings were saved.
settings.protectRoutesHint: Keeps the host's own default route and name servers. A profile can override this on its own.
settings.maxAttemptsHint: Zero never gives up. Authentication failures are not retried, because the same credentials would be refused again.
settings.reconnectDelay: Delay before the first retry, in seconds
settings.restoreOnStart: Reconnect the tunnels that were up when the application closed
settings.hotkeyHint: Shortcuts work while another application has the focus. A combination another application already owns is reported here rather than failing silently.
settings.notificationsHint: With many tunnels open, one message per event becomes noise. Turn off the ones you do not act on.
settings.rememberByDefault: Tick remember by default in the prompt
settings.credentialsHint:
Credentials are protected by the operating system and are readable only by this account on this machine. They never enter the profile database or an export.

Stored credentials are used without asking, so a profile connected daily never prompts. A connection the server refuses forgets what was stored and asks again, saying that the previous attempt was rejected. To change them before that happens, use Sign in again on the profile.
settings.openVpnPathHint: Leave empty to use the installed one
settings.conflictNotSaved: Two shortcuts use the same combination. Nothing was saved.
settings.transferHint: The import wizard reads .ovpn files, folders, ZIP archives and .ovppkg packages. Export writes plain configurations, or one encrypted package that carries a whole set to another machine.
settings.reloadProfilesHint: The list keeps itself current for anything done in this window. Reload it after the store was changed from somewhere else, such as the ovp command in a terminal.
settings.profilesReloaded: The profile list was read again.
settings.diagnosticsHint: Collects the environment report, the logs and a profile listing into one archive for a support request. Configurations and credentials are never included.
settings.diagnosticsPrivacy: A bundle is not anonymous. It contains profile names, remote host names and ports, file paths that include your Windows user name, and log lines that mention the same. It never contains configurations, private keys or credentials. Read it before sending it on.
settings.diagnosticsPrivacy@macos: A bundle is not anonymous. It contains profile names, remote host names and ports, file paths that include your macOS user name, and log lines that mention the same. It never contains configurations, private keys or credentials. Read it before sending it on.
settings.logRetention: Keep log files for, in days
settings.logMaximum: Keep log files up to, in megabytes
settings.logRetentionHint: One file is written per hour. Files older than the days above are removed, and so are the oldest files once all of them together reach the size above. Zero turns either limit off. A log names profiles, hosts and file paths that include your user name, so a short retention is the safer default.
settings.checkForUpdates: Look for a newer release when the application starts
settings.checkForUpdatesHint: This is the only thing here that contacts a network you did not ask it to. It reads the release list of the repository below from api.github.com, without credentials, and reports what it found. Nothing is downloaded and nothing is installed.

editor.title: Profile
editor.name: Name
editor.moreRemotes: This configuration names {0} servers, which OpenVPN tries in turn. The form changes the first; the plain text shows all of them.
editor.connectedNotice: This profile is connected. A changed configuration takes effect the next time it connects.
editor.slotHint: A slot binds this profile to the matching connect shortcut.
editor.keysHint: Paste each one including its BEGIN and END lines. An empty field removes that part from the configuration.
editor.plainHint: The whole configuration as OpenVPN reads it. It contains the private key, so treat it like a password.
editor.deleteConfirm: This removes the profile and its history. It cannot be undone.
editor.fixIssues: Nothing was saved. Fix what is marked in red first, because OpenVPN would refuse the configuration as it is.

issue.PortRequired: A port from 1 to 65535 is required.
issue.NoRemote: The configuration names no server. Add a line such as: remote vpn.example.com 1194 udp
issue.InvalidPort: '{0}' is not a port. A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
issue.InvalidProtocol: '{0}' is not a protocol a client can use. Use udp or tcp.
issue.NoServerVerification: Nothing verifies the server: there is no CA certificate and no ca, capath, pkcs12 or peer-fingerprint line. OpenVPN refuses to start without one.
issue.UnclosedBlock: The <{0}> block is opened here and never closed. Add </{0}> after its last line.
issue.StrayClosingTag: </{0}> closes a block that was never opened.
issue.NotACertificate: The <{0}> block does not hold a certificate. It has to run from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.
issue.NotAPrivateKey: The <{0}> block does not hold a private key. It has to run from a -----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY----- line to the matching END line.
issue.NotAStaticKey: The <{0}> block does not hold an OpenVPN static key. It has to run from -----BEGIN OpenVPN Static key V1----- to the matching END line.
issue.NotATlsCryptV2Key: The <{0}> block does not hold a tls-crypt-v2 client key.
issue.ExternalFile: {0} refers to the file '{1}', which a stored profile cannot reach. Paste its contents as a <{0}> block instead.
issue.ScriptDirective: {0} runs a program. The interactive service refuses that for callers it does not authorise, so the connection may be refused.
issue.ScriptDirective@macos: {0} runs a program. OpenVPN runs as root on macOS, so the helper refuses the configuration and it cannot be connected.

tags.help: Tags are how a profile set is organised. A profile can carry as many as it needs, the sidebar lists them, and the search box matches them along with the name and the host. Separate several with commas.

export.title: Export
export.packageHint: A package carries the selected profiles with their tags, and whichever of the shortcuts, the settings and the saved sign ins you include, in one encrypted file. It is the way to move a set to another machine.
export.configurationsHint: Plain configurations carry their private keys inline and cannot be encrypted, because OpenVPN has to read them. Treat the result as credentials.
export.passphraseRequired: A package is always encrypted, so a passphrase is required.
export.passphraseMismatch: The two entries do not match.
export.packageWrittenParts: {0} profile(s), {1} saved sign in(s), {2} shortcut(s), settings: {3}. Written to {4}.
export.includeSettingsHint: Language, appearance, connections, notifications, credentials and the advanced options. Window positions, the OpenVPN path, autostart and a shared library stay with this machine.
export.credentialsNone: None of the selected profiles has a saved sign in, so there is nothing to carry. A sign in is saved when a connection asks for one and the prompt is told to remember it.
export.credentialsAvailable: {0} saved sign in(s) belong to the selected profiles.
export.credentialsWarning: Anyone who has this file and its passphrase can connect as you. Send the passphrase separately from the package, and use the credentials page in the settings to clear what is stored if that is not what you want.

library.hint: Keeps the profiles and their saved sign ins in one encrypted file that several machines use together, for example in a folder OneDrive synchronises. Every machine keeps working with its own copy when the file cannot be reached, and catches up afterwards. Favourites, shortcuts, settings and history stay with each machine. The passphrase is asked for once per machine and kept in the operating system's protected storage.
library.leaveConfirm: The profiles stay on this machine and stop following the shared file. The passphrase is removed from this machine. The shared file itself is left as it is for everyone else.
library.left: This machine no longer uses the shared library. Its profiles stay here.
library.joinMessage: Enter the passphrase of {0}. The profiles in it are combined with the ones on this machine, and from then on both follow each other.
library.createMessage: {0} is written with every profile and saved sign in of this machine. Choose the passphrase every other machine will need, and pass it on separately from the file.
library.enterPassphraseMessage: The shared library needs its passphrase on this machine. It is asked for once and then kept in the operating system's protected storage.
library.changePassphraseMessage: The shared file is written again with the new passphrase, and every other machine asks for it the next time it synchronises. Somebody who knows only the old one cannot open anything written from now on.
library.passphraseWrong: The passphrase does not open the shared file, or the file was altered.
library.exists: A file already exists there. Use it as an existing library instead, or choose another name.
library.notALibrary: The file is not a shared library. {0}
library.unreachable: The shared file cannot be reached. {0}
library.waiting: Changes made here since {0} are waiting to be written to it.
library.reconciled: Shared library: {0} added, {1} changed, {2} removed, {3} sign in(s) updated.
library.lockedBy: {0} is writing to the shared file. This machine tries again shortly.
library.conflictCopies: The sync client left copies of the shared file beside it, which were read as well and can be deleted: {0}

conflict.bothKeptHere: {0} was changed here and on another machine. The same setting differed, and the change made here was later, so it was kept.
conflict.bothKeptThere: {0} was changed here and on another machine. The same setting differed, and the other change was later, so it replaced the one made here.
conflict.changedHereDeletedThere: {0} was removed on another machine after it was changed here, so it was kept and is shared again.
conflict.deletedHereChangedThere: {0} was removed here, but another machine changed it afterwards, so it is back.
conflict.more: {0} more profile(s) had a conflict of the same kind.

condition.Locked: Another machine is writing to the shared file. This machine tries again shortly.
condition.TooNew: A newer version of OpenVpnPilot wrote the shared file. Update this machine to keep synchronising.
condition.Damaged: The shared file opened but could not be read. {0}
condition.Failed: Synchronising with the shared file failed. {0}
